datasets.name: Mainsah et al. 2025 — bigP3BCI: An Open, Diverse and Machine Learning Ready P300-based Brain-Computer Interface Dataset (Study J)
datasets.description: Study J of the bigP3BCI collection, which provides EEG recordings from 20 healthy participants using a P300-based speller. The task used a 9x8 character grid with a performance-based row-column paradigm, and 16 EEG channels were recorded at 256 Hz. Target and non-target flash events are annotated with HED tags, and the dataset supports machine-learning benchmarking of P300 brain-computer interfaces.
datasets.authors: Boyla Mainsah, Chance Fleeting, Thomas Balmat, Eric Sellers, Leslie Collins

datasets.name: Stieger et al. 2021 — Continuous sensorimotor rhythm based brain computer interface learning in a large population
datasets.description: A large, longitudinal EEG dataset collected while 62 healthy adults learned to control a sensorimotor rhythm-based brain-computer interface. Participants completed 7-11 online training sessions of continuous cursor control using motor imagery of the left hand, right hand, both hands, and rest. In total the dataset comprises 598 sessions and over 250,000 trials, offering a resource for designing and evaluating BCI algorithms and for studying BCI learning.
datasets.authors: James R. Stieger, Stephen A. Engel, Bin He

datasets.name: Lee et al. 2019 (Motor Imagery) — EEG dataset and OpenBMI toolbox for three BCI paradigms: an investigation into BCI illiteracy
datasets.description: A motor imagery EEG dataset from 54 healthy participants performing binary left/right hand grasping imagery across two sessions on different days. Recordings were made with 62 EEG channels plus 4 EMG channels at 1000 Hz. The data belong to a larger multi-paradigm BCI collection (MI, ERP, SSVEP) used to investigate BCI illiteracy and variation in decoding performance across subjects and sessions.
datasets.authors: Min-Ho Lee, O-Yeon Kwon, Yong-Jeong Kim, Hong-Kyung Kim, Young-Eun Lee, John Williamson, Siamac Fazli, Seong-Whan Lee

datasets.name: Mainsah et al. 2025 — bigP3BCI: An Open, Diverse and Machine Learning Ready P300-based Brain-Computer Interface Dataset (Study R)
datasets.description: This dataset is Study R of bigP3BCI, a large open P300-based brain-computer interface collection. It contains 32-channel EEG recorded from 20 participants over two sessions each, using a 9x8 multi-face speller grid with target and non-target flashes. The data are standardized in BIDS and prepared for machine learning and benchmarking of P300 speller decoding.
datasets.authors: Boyla Mainsah, Chance Fleeting, Thomas Balmat, Eric Sellers, Leslie Collins

datasets.name: Brandl et al. 2020 — Motor Imagery Under Distraction: An Open Access BCI Dataset
datasets.description: An open-access EEG dataset of a motor imagery brain-computer interface experiment conducted under distraction. Sixteen healthy participants performed left- versus right-hand motor imagery, first in a calibration run and then in feedback runs under six conditions: no distraction, eyes closed, news listening, number search, flickering video, and vibro-tactile stimulation. Recordings comprise 63 EEG channels at 1000 Hz and 504 trials per subject.
datasets.authors: Stephanie Brandl, Benjamin Blankertz, Tobias Dahne

datasets.name: Mainsah et al. 2025 — bigP3BCI: An Open, Diverse and Machine Learning Ready P300-based Brain-Computer Interface Dataset (Study C)
datasets.description: Study C of the bigP3BCI collection, which contains EEG recordings from 19 healthy participants using a 6x6 checkerboard P300 speller paradigm with error-related negativity (ERN). Data were recorded with 32 channels at 256 Hz and annotated with target and non-target events using HED. bigP3BCI is a large, diverse, machine-learning-ready public P300 BCI dataset spanning many studies.
datasets.authors: Boyla Mainsah, Chance Fleeting, Thomas Balmat, Eric Sellers, Leslie Collins

datasets.name: Lee et al. 2019 (ERP) — EEG dataset and OpenBMI toolbox for three BCI paradigms: an investigation into BCI illiteracy
datasets.description: EEG recordings from 54 healthy participants performing a 36-symbol ERP (P300) row-column speller task with face stimuli, collected over two sessions with offline training and online copy-spelling test phases. Data were recorded at 1000 Hz from 62 EEG channels plus 4 additional EMG channels. The dataset is part of a three-paradigm BCI collection (ERP, SSVEP, motor imagery) created to investigate BCI illiteracy and distributed with the OpenBMI toolbox.
datasets.authors: Min-Ho Lee, O-Yeon Kwon, Yong-Jeong Kim, Hong-Kyung Kim, Young-Eun Lee, John Williamson, Siamac Fazli, Seong-Whan Lee

datasets.name: Mainsah et al. 2025 — bigP3BCI: An Open, Diverse and Machine Learning Ready P300-based Brain-Computer Interface Dataset (Study Q)
datasets.description: This dataset contains EEG recordings from 36 participants with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (Study Q of the bigP3BCI collection) performing a P300-based speller task with a 6x6 character grid and color intensification. Data were recorded across three sessions per subject with 32 EEG channels at 256 Hz. It is a BIDS-formatted derivative of the PhysioNet bigP3BCI release, intended for machine learning and benchmarking of P300 brain-computer interfaces.
datasets.authors: Boyla Mainsah, Chance Fleeting, Thomas Balmat, Eric Sellers, Leslie Collins

datasets.name: Mainsah et al. 2025 — bigP3BCI: An Open, Diverse and Machine Learning Ready P300-based Brain-Computer Interface Dataset (Study S2)
datasets.description: This dataset contains EEG recordings from 24 healthy participants in Study S2 of bigP3BCI, a large open P300-based brain-computer interface collection. Participants used a 9x8 character grid speller with a house/tool stimulus paradigm, with target and non-target events annotated using HED. Data were recorded at 256 Hz from 32 channels and are provided in a machine-learning-ready BIDS format via MOABB.
datasets.authors: Boyla Mainsah, Chance Fleeting, Thomas Balmat, Eric Sellers, Leslie Collins

datasets.name: Guttmann-Flury et al. 2025 (SSVEP) — Dataset combining EEG, eye-tracking, and high-speed video for ocular activity analysis across BCI paradigms
datasets.description: A multimodal SSVEP dataset of 64-channel EEG, an EOG channel, and stimulus markers recorded from 31 healthy participants over up to 3 sessions each (63 sessions in total). Participants viewed LED stimuli flickering at four frequencies in a 4-class SSVEP paradigm (48 trials per session). It is the SSVEP component of a larger resource combining EEG, eye-tracking, and high-speed video for ocular activity analysis across BCI paradigms, and is formatted for use with MOABB.
datasets.authors: Eva Guttmann-Flury, Xinjun Sheng, Xiangyang Zhu

datasets.name: Mainsah et al. 2025 — bigP3BCI: An Open, Diverse and Machine Learning Ready P300-based Brain-Computer Interface Dataset (Study O)
datasets.description: This dataset is Study O of bigP3BCI, a large open collection of P300-based brain-computer interface EEG recordings. It contains 32-channel EEG from 18 participants with ALS, each recorded over two sessions while using a 9x8 character speller with a supervised checkerboard stimulus paradigm. Target and non-target flashes are annotated with HED tags, and the data are formatted for machine learning and benchmarking.
datasets.authors: Boyla Mainsah, Chance Fleeting, Thomas Balmat, Eric Sellers, Leslie Collins

datasets.name: Mainsah et al. 2025 — bigP3BCI: An Open, Diverse and Machine Learning Ready P300-based Brain-Computer Interface Dataset (Study D)
datasets.description: Study D of the bigP3BCI collection, comprising 32-channel EEG recordings from 17 healthy participants using a P300-based speller with a 6x6 character grid and dynamic row-column stimulus presentation. Data were recorded in a single session per subject with online feedback, and events are labeled as target or non-target flashes. The dataset is a BIDS-formatted derivative of the PhysioNet bigP3BCI release, intended for machine learning and BCI benchmarking.
datasets.authors: Boyla Mainsah, Chance Fleeting, Thomas Balmat, Eric Sellers, Leslie Collins

datasets.name: Mainsah et al. 2025 — bigP3BCI: An Open, Diverse and Machine Learning Ready P300-based Brain-Computer Interface Dataset (Study G)
datasets.description: This dataset contains P300-based brain-computer interface EEG recordings from 20 healthy participants in Study G of the bigP3BCI collection. Participants used a 9x8 character grid speller with checkerboard/dynamic stimulus presentation. Sixteen EEG channels were recorded at 256 Hz, with target and non-target events annotated using HED. The data are a MOABB-derived BIDS version of the original PhysioNet bigP3BCI resource.
datasets.authors: Boyla Mainsah, Chance Fleeting, Thomas Balmat, Eric Sellers, Leslie Collins

datasets.name: Shin et al. 2017 (Experiment B) — Open Access Dataset for EEG+NIRS Single-Trial Classification
datasets.description: Open-access EEG dataset from Experiment B of Shin et al. (2017), recorded alongside NIRS for hybrid brain-computer interface research. 29 healthy participants performed cued mental arithmetic (serial subtraction) versus resting-baseline trials across alternating sessions. This derivative release contains preprocessed 30-channel EEG (CAR, 0.5-50 Hz bandpass, ICA-based EOG rejection, 200 Hz) with HED event annotations, formatted for benchmarking single-trial classification in MOABB.
datasets.authors: Jaeyoung Shin, Alexander von Lühmann, Benjamin Blankertz, Do-Won Kim, Jichai Jeong, Han-Jeong Hwang, Klaus-Robert Müller

datasets.name: Sosulski et al. 2019 — Online Optimization of Stimulation Speed in an Auditory Brain-Computer Interface under Time Constraints
datasets.description: EEG recordings from 13 healthy participants performing an auditory oddball (P300) paradigm with target (1000 Hz) and non-target (500 Hz) tones presented at varying stimulus onset asynchronies (60-600 ms). The data were collected to evaluate closed-loop Bayesian optimization and random search for selecting individually optimal stimulation speed in an auditory brain-computer interface. The dataset contains 31-channel EEG sampled at 1000 Hz, covering both an optimization part and a validation part.
datasets.authors: Jan Sosulski, David Hübner, Aaron Klein, Michael Tangermann

datasets.name: Guttmann-Flury et al. 2025 (Motor Imagery) — Dataset combining EEG, eye-tracking, and high-speed video for ocular activity analysis across BCI paradigms
datasets.description: This dataset contains 64-channel EEG recorded from 31 healthy participants performing a two-class (left vs. right hand) motor imagery task. Each participant completed up to three sessions of 40 trials. The recordings are part of a multimodal collection that also includes eye-tracking and high-speed video, intended for analyzing ocular activity across BCI paradigms. Events are annotated with HED, and the data are organized in BIDS format via MOABB.
datasets.authors: Eva Guttmann-Flury, Xinjun Sheng, Xiangyang Zhu

datasets.name: Vaineau, Barachant & Andreev 2013 — Brain Invaders Adaptive versus Non-Adaptive P300 Brain-Computer Interface dataset (BI2013a)
datasets.description: EEG recordings from 24 healthy participants performing a visual P300 Brain-Computer Interface task based on the Brain Invaders video game. The experiment compared a P300 BCI with and without adaptive calibration using Riemannian geometry. Data were recorded with 16 wet electrodes at GIPSA-lab, Grenoble, in 2013, across 8 sessions per subject with randomised adaptive and non-adaptive runs.
datasets.authors: E. Vaineau, A. Barachant, A. Andreev, P. Rodrigues, G. Cattan, M. Congedo

datasets.name: Van Veen, Barachant & Andreev 2012 — Building Brain Invaders: EEG data of an experimental validation (BI2012)
datasets.description: EEG recordings from 25 healthy volunteers playing Brain Invaders, a visual P300 brain-computer interface inspired by the video game Space Invaders. Data were acquired with 16 electrodes at GIPSA-lab (Grenoble, France) in 2012, using a training-test design with Target and NonTarget flashes of alien groups. This BIDS version was generated from the original Zenodo deposit through MOABB.
datasets.authors: G.F.P. Van Veen, A. Barachant, A. Andreev, G. Cattan, P. Rodrigues, M. Congedo

datasets.name: The Brain, Body, and Behaviour Dataset (1.0.0) - Experiment 3
datasets.description: Multimodal recordings from 29 participants who watched six educational videos in two conditions: an attentive session with comprehension questions afterward (intentional learning), and a distracted session in which they counted backwards by sevens. The recordings include EEG, ECG, EOG, gaze, pupil size, blinks, saccades, and head position. The videos cover three presentation styles, which lets the dataset be used to study how video design affects attention and learning. Questionnaire data include video-related knowledge and memory questions and the ASRS adult ADHD symptom checklist.
datasets.authors: Jens Madsen, Nikhil Kuppa, Lucas Parra

datasets.name: The Brain, Body, and Behaviour Dataset (1.0.0) - Experiment 2
datasets.description: Multimodal dataset of 31 participants who watched five informative educational videos under two conditions: an attentive condition followed by factual multiple-choice questions, and a distracted condition in which they silently counted backwards in steps of 7. Recordings include EEG, EOG, ECG, gaze, pupil size, blinks, saccades, and head motion. Questionnaires on stimulus knowledge and adult ADHD symptoms (ASRS) accompany the recordings. The experiment targets incidental learning and attention during video watching.
datasets.authors: Jens Madsen, Nikhil Kuppa, Lucas Parra

datasets.name: Dreyer et al. 2023 — A large EEG database with users' profile information for motor imagery brain-computer interface research
datasets.description: A large EEG database from 87 healthy participants recorded during a single-day motor imagery brain-computer interface (BCI) experiment. The data are organized into three datasets (A, B, C) that share one Graz-protocol task, left- versus right-hand motor imagery, with 240 trials per participant (over 20,800 trials in total). It also provides demographic, personality and cognitive-trait information, which supports studies of how user profiles relate to BCI performance and cross-user classification algorithms.
datasets.authors: Pauline Dreyer, Aline Roc, Léa Pillette, Sébastien Rimbert, Fabien Lotte

datasets.name: PURSUE N400 Word Processing
datasets.description: EEG dataset from the PURSUE project containing an N400 word processing task, recorded from participants at three primarily undergraduate institutions (Southern California, Massachusetts, and Virginia) in 2017 and 2018. The task design follows the ERP CORE paradigm. The dataset supports event-related potential research on semantic word processing.
datasets.authors: Couperus, J.W., Bukach, C.M., Reed, C.L.

datasets.name: PURSUE N2pc Visual Search
datasets.description: EEG dataset from a visual search task eliciting the N2pc event-related potential, collected as part of the PURSUE project. Participants were recruited at three primarily undergraduate institutions (Southern California, Massachusetts, and Virginia) in 2017 and 2018. The task follows the ERP CORE paradigm.
datasets.authors: Couperus, J.W., Bukach, C.M., Reed, C.L.

datasets.name: PURSUE N170 Face Perception
datasets.description: EEG dataset from the PURSUE project of a face perception task designed to elicit the N170 event-related potential. Data were collected from participants at three primarily undergraduate institutions in Southern California, Massachusetts, and Virginia during 2017 and 2018. The task follows the ERP CORE paradigm, and the dataset includes participant race information.
datasets.authors: Couperus, J.W., Bukach, C.M., Reed,C.L.

datasets.name: PURSUE MMN Auditory Oddball
datasets.description: EEG dataset from a passive auditory oddball (mismatch negativity) experiment conducted as part of the PURSUE project. Data were collected from participants at three primarily undergraduate institutions in Southern California, Massachusetts, and Virginia during 2017 and 2018. The task follows the ERP CORE paradigm.
datasets.authors: Couperus, J.W., Bukach, C.M., Reed, C.L.

datasets.name: PURSUE LRP/ERN Flanker
datasets.description: EEG dataset from the PURSUE project containing a flanker task designed to elicit the lateralized readiness potential (LRP) and error-related negativity (ERN). Data were collected in 2017 and 2018 from participants at three primarily undergraduate institutions in Southern California, Massachusetts, and Virginia. The task follows the ERP CORE paradigm.
datasets.authors: Couperus, J.W., Bukach, C.M., Reed, C.L.

datasets.name: PURSUE P300 Visual Oddball
datasets.description: EEG dataset of a visual oddball (P300) task from the PURSUE project, collected in 2017 and 2018 from participants at three primarily undergraduate institutions in Southern California, Massachusetts, and Virginia. The task design follows the ERP CORE paradigm, and the dataset includes participant demographic information such as race.
datasets.authors: Couperus, J.W., Bukach, C.M., Reed, C.L.

datasets.name: BNCI 2022-001 EEG Correlates of Difficulty Level dataset
datasets.description: EEG recordings from 13 healthy participants who piloted a simulated drone through circular waypoints at varying difficulty levels using a joystick. The dataset includes an offline session with a v-shaped difficulty design and two online sessions in which subjective difficulty was decoded from EEG to support closed-loop adaptation of task difficulty. Data were recorded with a 64-channel Biosemi ActiveTwo system and are provided preprocessed in BIDS format via the MOABB collection (BNCI 2022-001).
datasets.authors: Ping-Keng Jao, Ricardo Chavarriaga, Jose del R. Millan

datasets.name: BigP3BCI Study L — 6x6 multi-paradigm (11 ALS subjects)
datasets.description: EEG recordings from 11 participants with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) performing a P300-based brain-computer interface speller task on a 6x6 character grid with multiple stimulus paradigms. The data are Study L of the larger bigP3BCI collection, which spans about 267 subjects across 20 studies. This BIDS derivative was generated with MOABB and includes HED event annotations for target and non-target stimuli.
datasets.authors: Boyla Mainsah, Chance Fleeting, Thomas Balmat, Eric Sellers, Leslie Collins

datasets.name: BigP3BCI Study S1 — 9x8 face/house paradigm (10 healthy subjects)
datasets.description: This dataset contains 32-channel EEG recordings from 10 healthy participants performing a P300-based brain-computer interface speller task. It uses a 9x8 character grid with a face/house stimulus paradigm and is Study S1 of the larger bigP3BCI collection. Target and non-target events are annotated with HED tags, and the data support P300 detection and speller research.
datasets.authors: Boyla Mainsah, Chance Fleeting, Thomas Balmat, Eric Sellers, Leslie Collins

datasets.name: Multi-day MI-BCI dataset (WBCIC-SHU) from Yang et al 2025
datasets.description: A multi-day motor imagery brain-computer interface EEG dataset recorded from 51 healthy, BCI-naive participants over three sessions on different days. Participants performed left-hand and right-hand motor imagery (2-class, 51 subjects), and a subset of 11 subjects also performed a 3-class paradigm that added foot-hooking. Recordings used 59 EEG channels plus ECG and EOG at 1000 Hz. The data are provided in BIDS format with HED event annotations and benchmark classification results (CSP, FBCSP, EEGNet, deepConvNet, FBCNet).
datasets.authors: Banghua Yang, Fenqi Rong, Yunlong Xie, Du Li, Jiayang Zhang, Fu Li, Guangming Shi, Xiaorong Gao

datasets.name: Motor Imagery dataset from Cho et al 2017
datasets.description: A motor imagery brain-computer interface EEG dataset from 52 healthy subjects performing left- and right-hand kinesthetic finger movement imagery. Recordings include 64-channel EEG and 4 EMG channels sampled at 512 Hz. They are accompanied by psychological and physiological questionnaires, 3D electrode locations, and non-task-related states. This BIDS derivative was generated with MOABB from the original GigaDB deposit.
datasets.authors: Hohyun Cho, Minkyu Ahn, Sangtae Ahn, Moonyoung Kwon, Sung Chan Jun

datasets.name: P300 dataset BI2014a from a "Brain Invaders" experiment
datasets.description: EEG recordings from a visual P300 Brain-Computer Interface videogame, Brain Invaders, collected at GIPSA-lab (Grenoble, France) in 2014. Participants played a game using an oddball paradigm on a grid of 36 symbols while 16 dry electrodes recorded their EEG, with up to three game sessions per participant. The dataset was designed to study the viability of a calibration-less P300-based BCI with dry electrodes.
datasets.authors: Louis Korczowski, Ekaterina Ostaschenko, Anton Andreev, Grégoire Cattan, Pedro Luiz Coelho Rodrigues, Violette Gautheret, Marco Congedo

datasets.name: BNCI 2016-002 Emergency Braking during Simulated Driving dataset
datasets.description: EEG, EMG and vehicle-dynamics recordings from 15 healthy participants who drove a simulated racing car while following a lead vehicle that occasionally braked abruptly. The dataset supports detection of emergency-braking intention from brain and muscle signals before the behavioral response, with target and non-target events for event-related potential and BCI analyses. It is a preprocessed BIDS derivative of the BNCI Horizon 2016-002 collection, distributed via MOABB.
datasets.authors: Stefan Haufe, Matthias S Treder, Manfred F Gugler, Max Sagebaum, Gabriel Curio, Benjamin Blankertz

datasets.name: Visual imagery EEG dataset from Gao et al 2026
datasets.description: This dataset contains 32-channel EEG recorded from 22 healthy participants performing visual imagery of ten cued items: animals (dog, bird, fish), geometric figures (pentagram, square, circle), and objects (scissor, watch, cup, chair). Each participant completed up to two sessions of three runs, giving 16,800 trials in total. It is intended for developing visual imagery-based brain-computer interfaces and is distributed in BIDS format with HED event annotations.
datasets.authors: Jing'ao Gao, Yao Liu, Zhengshuang Li, Kaixin Huang, Fan Wang, Jiaping Xu, Lei Zhao, Tianwen Li, Yunfa Fu

datasets.name: Checkerboard m-sequence-based c-VEP dataset from
datasets.description: An EEG dataset of code-modulated visual evoked potentials (c-VEP) elicited by checkerboard-pattern m-sequence stimuli, recorded from 16 healthy participants with 16 channels at 256 Hz. It was collected to evaluate how the spatial frequency of visual stimuli affects the performance and user experience of c-VEP-based brain-computer interfaces. Each stimulus condition is stored as a separate session, with three runs per session (two for training, one for testing). The data are distributed in BIDS format via MOABB.
datasets.authors: Álvaro Fernández-Rodríguez, Víctor Martínez-Cagigal, Eduardo Santamaría-Vázquez, Ricardo Ron-Angevin, Roberto Hornero

datasets.name: Dataset of an EEG-based BCI experiment in Virtual Reality using P300
datasets.description: EEG recordings from 21 healthy participants performing a visual P300 brain-computer interface speller task, with each participant completing one session on a personal computer and one in virtual reality using a passive smartphone-based head-mounted display. Signals were recorded from 16 electrodes at 512 Hz. The dataset supports comparison of P300-based BCI performance, physiological responses, and user experience between the PC and VR conditions.
datasets.authors: Grégoire Cattan, Anton Andreev, Pedro Luiz Coelho Rodrigues, Marco Congedo

datasets.name: Eye-BCI multimodal MI/ME dataset from Guttmann-Flury et al 2025
datasets.description: A multimodal EEG dataset of motor imagery (MI) recorded from 31 healthy participants over up to three sessions each. Participants imagined left- and right-hand grasping in response to visual cues while 64-channel EEG plus EOG were recorded at 1000 Hz. This is a MOABB-derived version of the Eye-BCI dataset, which also includes eye-tracking and high-speed video for ocular activity analysis across BCI paradigms.
datasets.authors: Eva Guttmann-Flury, Xinjun Sheng, Xiangyang Zhu

datasets.name: BNCI 2015-009 AMUSE (Auditory Multi-class Spatial ERP) dataset
datasets.description: EEG recordings from 21 participants performing an offline auditory spatial oddball task for a multi-class brain-computer interface (AMUSE). Five frontal speakers presented unique auditory stimuli under three conditions that varied inter-stimulus interval and speaker configuration, and participants attended to target directions. The data were used to evaluate P300-based spelling and communication paradigms, and are distributed here in preprocessed form through MOABB.
datasets.authors: Martijn Schreuder, Benjamin Blankertz, Michael Tangermann

datasets.name: P300 dataset from Hoffmann et al 2008
datasets.description: EEG recordings from eight participants, four with severe motor disabilities and four able-bodied, performing a P300-based brain-computer interface task for environment control. Participants silently counted flashes of a prescribed target image among six household-item images (television, telephone, lamp, door, window, radio) shown in random sequences. Data were recorded in four sessions of six runs each with a 32-channel Biosemi ActiveTwo system.
datasets.authors: Ulrich Hoffmann, Jean-Marc Vesin, Touradj Ebrahimi, Karin Diserens

datasets.name: Lower-limb MI dataset for knee pain patients from Zuo et al. 2025
datasets.description: EEG recordings from 30 knee pain patients performing a two-class lower-limb motor imagery task (left vs. right leg flexion/extension). Each participant completed 5 sessions of 100 cue-based trials, recorded with a 30-channel system at 500 Hz. The dataset supports brain-computer interface research for rehabilitation and benchmarking of classifiers such as CSP+LDA, FBCSP+SVM and EEGNet.
datasets.authors: Chongwen Zuo, Yi Yin, Haochong Wang, Zhiyang Zheng, Xiaoyan Ma, Yuan Yang, Jue Wang, Shan Wang, Zi-gang Huang, Chaoqun Ye

datasets.name: Gwilliams et al. 2023 — Introducing MEG-MASC: a high-quality magneto-encephalography dataset for evaluating natural speech processing
datasets.description: MEG-MASC provides raw magnetoencephalography recordings from 27 English speakers who listened to about two hours of naturalistic synthesized stories drawn from the Manually Annotated Sub-Corpus (MASC), intermixed with word lists and comprehension questions. Each participant completed two identical sessions. Word and phoneme onsets and offsets are time-stamped in the BIDS events files, which makes the dataset a benchmark for large-scale encoding and decoding analyses of temporally resolved brain responses to speech.
datasets.authors: Laura Gwilliams, Graham Flick, Alec Marantz, Liina Pylkkänen, David Poeppel, Jean-Rémi King

datasets.name: Nieuwland et al. 2018: Multi-site N400 Replication Study
datasets.description: A large-scale (N=356) multi-laboratory EEG replication of DeLong, Urbach & Kutas (2005), testing whether readers pre-activate the phonological form of upcoming nouns during sentence comprehension. Participants at nine UK laboratories read sentences word by word, with indefinite articles (a/an) preceding expected or unexpected nouns. The data show reliable N400 effects on target nouns but no statistically significant effect on the preceding articles, which challenges strong accounts of prediction. The release includes all subjects with available raw data and a flag marking those included in the original paper's analyses.
datasets.authors: Mante S. Nieuwland, Stephen Politzer-Ahles, Evelien Heyselaar, Katrien Segaert, Emily Darley, Nina Kazanina, Sarah Von Grebmer Zu Wolfsthurn, Federica Bartolozzi, Vita Kogan, Aine Ito, Diane Mézière, Dale J. Barr, Guillaume A. Rousselet, Heather J. Ferguson, Simon Busch-Moreno, Xiao Fu, Jyrki Tuomainen, Eugenia Kulakova, E. Matthew Husband, David I. Donaldson, Zdenko Kohút, Shirley-Ann Rueschemeyer, Falk Huettig

datasets.name: Eye-BCI Motor Execution dataset from Guttmann-Flury et al 2025
datasets.description: A BIDS-formatted EEG dataset of two-class hand-grasping motor tasks (left vs. right hand) from 31 healthy participants, recorded with a 64-channel Neuroscan system at 1000 Hz across up to three sessions of 40 trials each. It is a derivative of the multi-paradigm Eye-BCI dataset, which combines EEG, eye-tracking and high-speed video for ocular activity analysis. It is provided through MOABB for benchmarking motor-related brain-computer interface decoding.
datasets.authors: Eva Guttmann-Flury, Xinjun Sheng, Xiangyang Zhu

datasets.name: PhysioNet 2018 Challenge: Sleep Arousal Detection PSG (Training)
datasets.description: This dataset contains 1,983 overnight polysomnography recordings from patients at the Massachusetts General Hospital sleep laboratory, most of whom were evaluated for suspected sleep disorders such as obstructive sleep apnea. It was created for the PhysioNet/Computing in Cardiology Challenge 2018 on automatic detection of sleep arousals. The training set (994 subjects) includes expert annotations of sleep stages, respiratory events and arousals, while the test set (989 subjects) contains signals only. Recordings comprise EEG, EOG, EMG, respiratory effort, airflow, SpO2 and ECG channels sampled at 200 Hz.
datasets.authors: Mohammad M. Ghassemi, Benjamin E. Moody, Li-wei H. Lehman, Christopher Song, Qiao Li, Haoqi Sun, Roger G. Mark, M. Brandon Westover, Gari D. Clifford
datasets.license: Open Data Commons Attribution License v1.0
datasets.placement_scheme: 10-20 subset (F3, F4, C3, C4, O1, O2)

datasets.name: Electric light control experiment (15 subjects, 4 classes, 31 EEG ch)
datasets.description: EEG recordings from 15 healthy participants performing a visual P300 oddball paradigm designed for brain-computer interface control of home appliances, specifically an electric light with four selectable classes. Data were acquired with 31 active EEG channels at 500 Hz while stimuli were flashed on an LCD display, and include training and online testing blocks per subject. The dataset supports development and benchmarking of ERP-based BCIs and inter-subject transfer learning.
datasets.authors: Jongmin Lee, Minju Kim, Dojin Heo, Jongsu Kim, Min-Ki Kim, Taejun Lee, Jongwoo Park, HyunYoung Kim, Minho Hwang, Laehyun Kim, Sung-Phil Kim

datasets.name: Air conditioner control experiment (10 subjects, 4 classes, 25 EEG ch)
datasets.description: EEG recordings from 10 healthy participants performing an online visual P300 brain-computer interface task to control a home air conditioner. A 4-class oddball paradigm was presented on an LCD display, with 25 EEG channels recorded at 500 Hz. Each participant completed 50 training and 30 testing blocks, supporting research on ERP-based BCIs for home appliance control and inter-subject transfer learning.
datasets.authors: Jongmin Lee, Minju Kim, Dojin Heo, Jongsu Kim, Min-Ki Kim, Taejun Lee, Jongwoo Park, HyunYoung Kim, Minho Hwang, Laehyun Kim, Sung-Phil Kim

datasets.name: Alphawaves dataset
datasets.description: Resting-state EEG recordings from 19 healthy participants who alternated between eyes-closed and eyes-open conditions in 10-second trials. Data were acquired with a 16-channel g.tec g.USBamp system at 512 Hz to study posterior alpha-band (8-12 Hz) modulation. The dataset is distributed in BIDS format via MOABB and originates from the GIPSA-lab Alpha Waves dataset.
datasets.authors: Grégoire Cattan, Pedro Luiz Coelho Rodrigues, Marco Congedo

datasets.name: BNCI 2020-002 Attention Shift (Covert Spatial Attention) dataset
datasets.description: EEG recordings from 18 healthy participants performing a gaze-independent brain-computer interface task based on covert spatial attention shifts. Participants answered yes/no questions by shifting attention to a green or red cross while maintaining central fixation, and N2pc-related ERP responses were classified with canonical correlation analysis. The data were recorded with 30 EEG channels and 2 EOG channels at 250 Hz.
datasets.authors: Christoph Reichert, Igor Fabian Tellez Ceja, Catherine M. Sweeney-Reed, Hans-Jochen Heinze, Hermann Hinrichs, Stefan Dürschmid

datasets.name: BigP3BCI Study H — 9x8 checkerboard with gaze conditions (16 healthy subjects)
datasets.description: This dataset is Study H of the BigP3BCI collection, a P300-based brain-computer interface speller experiment. EEG was recorded from 16 healthy participants using a 9x8 checkerboard character grid under different gaze conditions. It is a MOABB-derived, BIDS-formatted version of the PhysioNet bigP3BCI release, with target and non-target stimulus events annotated using HED.
datasets.authors: Boyla Mainsah, Chance Fleeting, Thomas Balmat, Eric Sellers, Leslie Collins

datasets.name: P300 dataset BI2015b from a "Brain Invaders" experiment
datasets.description: EEG recordings from 44 participants playing Brain Invaders in a cooperative versus competitive multi-user setting (bi2015b). Brain Invaders is a visual P300 brain-computer interface videogame. The game uses an oddball paradigm on a grid of 36 aliens, with 1 target and 35 non-targets flashed in pseudo-random groups. Data were recorded with 32 wet electrodes at GIPSA-lab, Grenoble, in 2015.
datasets.authors: Louis Korczowski, Martine Cederhout, Anton Andreev, Grégoire Cattan, Pedro Luiz Coelho Rodrigues, Violette Gautheret, Marco Congedo

datasets.name: P300 dataset BI2015a from a "Brain Invaders" experiment
datasets.description: EEG recordings from 43 healthy participants playing Brain Invaders, a visual P300 brain-computer interface game based on an oddball paradigm with a grid of 36 symbols. Data were recorded with 32 wet electrodes across three sessions with flash durations of 50, 80 and 110 ms. The study examined the influence of flash duration on a calibration-less P300 BCI that used an adaptive Riemannian minimum distance to mean classifier. It was collected at GIPSA-lab, Grenoble, in 2015.
datasets.authors: Louis Korczowski, Martine Cederhout, Anton Andreev, Grégoire Cattan, Pedro Luiz Coelho Rodrigues, Violette Gautheret, Marco Congedo

datasets.name: P300 dataset BI2014b from a "Brain Invaders" experiment
datasets.description: EEG recordings from 38 subjects playing in pairs the multi-user version of Brain Invaders, a visual P300-based brain-computer interface using an oddball paradigm on a grid of 36 symbols. Data were acquired with 32 wet electrodes per subject during three randomized conditions (Solo1, Solo2, Collaboration), supporting research on inter-brain synchrony and collaborative BCI. The experiment was conducted at GIPSA-lab, Grenoble, France, in 2014.
datasets.authors: Louis Korczowski, Ekaterina Ostaschenko, Anton Andreev, Grégoire Cattan, Pedro Luiz Coelho Rodrigues, Violette Gautheret, Marco Congedo

datasets.name: c-VEP dataset from Thielen et al. (2021)
datasets.description: A code-modulated visual evoked potential (c-VEP) brain-computer interface dataset recorded from 30 healthy participants using 8 EEG electrodes at 512 Hz. Participants fixated on target cells in a 20-symbol grid while all cells flashed pseudo-random modulated Gold codes. The data support comparison of full-calibration, reduced-training and zero-training classification using a reconvolution encoding model.
datasets.authors: J Thielen, P Marsman, J Farquhar, P Desain

datasets.name: Television control experiment (30 subjects, 4 classes, 31 EEG ch)
datasets.description: EEG recordings from 30 healthy participants performing a visual P300 oddball paradigm for brain-computer interface control of a television. Data were acquired with 31 active electrodes at 500 Hz while participants selected among four home appliance control commands on an LCD display. Target and non-target flash events are annotated, with training and online testing blocks for each subject. The dataset supports research on ERP-based BCIs and inter-subject transfer learning.
datasets.authors: Jongmin Lee, Minju Kim, Dojin Heo, Jongsu Kim, Min-Ki Kim, Taejun Lee, Jongwoo Park, HyunYoung Kim, Minho Hwang, Laehyun Kim, Sung-Phil Kim

datasets.name: BNCI 2015-007 Motion VEP (mVEP) Speller dataset
datasets.description: EEG recordings from 16 healthy, BCI-naive participants using a motion visually evoked potential (mVEP) speller for gaze-independent communication. Three speller variants were compared: Overt Cake Speller, Covert Cake Speller, and Motion Center Speller. Each used a two-level selection among 30 symbols. The dataset includes practice, calibration, copy-spelling and free-spelling sessions with target and non-target events, recorded from 63 channels. It is a preprocessed derivative distributed in BIDS format.
datasets.authors: Sulamith Schaeff, Matthias Sebastian Treder, Bastian Venthur, Benjamin Blankertz

datasets.name: BCIAUT-P300 dataset for autism from Simoes et al 2020
datasets.description: EEG dataset from 15 autistic adolescents and adults who took part in a P300-based brain-computer interface joint-attention training in a virtual environment. Each participant completed 7 sessions, recorded with 8 EEG channels at 250 Hz while attending to flashing objects, with target and non-target events. The dataset serves as a multi-session, multi-subject benchmark for P300 BCI classification and is distributed in BIDS format via MOABB.
datasets.authors: Marco Simoes, Davide Borra, Eduardo Santamaria-Vazquez, Mayra Bittencourt-Villalpando, Dominik Krzeminski, Aleksandar Miladinovic, Carlos Amaral, Bruno Direito, Miguel Castelo-Branco

datasets.name: Motor imagery + spatial attention dataset from Forenzo & He 2023
datasets.description: EEG dataset from 25 healthy participants performing a cursor-control brain-computer interface task across five sessions. The study combined motor imagery, overt spatial attention, and simultaneous motor imagery with spatial attention (MIOSA), with online visual cursor feedback. Recordings used 64 channels at 1000 Hz, and this release provides left-hand versus right-hand motor imagery trials.
datasets.authors: Dylan Forenzo, Yixuan Liu, Jeehyun Kim, Yidan Ding, Taehyung Yoon, Bin He

datasets.name: Door lock control experiment (15 subjects, 4 classes, 31 EEG ch)
datasets.description: EEG recordings from 15 healthy participants performing a P300-based brain-computer interface task for controlling a home appliance, specifically a door lock. Data were acquired with 31 active EEG channels at 500 Hz during a four-class visual oddball paradigm presented on an LCD display, with target and non-target flashes. Each subject completed 50 training and 30 testing blocks, including online testing with visual feedback.
datasets.authors: Jongmin Lee, Minju Kim, Dojin Heo, Jongsu Kim, Min-Ki Kim, Taejun Lee, Jongwoo Park, HyunYoung Kim, Minho Hwang, Laehyun Kim, Sung-Phil Kim

datasets.name: Kojima et al. 2024 (Dataset B) — Four-class ASME BCI: investigation of the feasibility and comparison of two strategies for multiclassing
datasets.description: EEG dataset from 15 healthy participants performing a four-class auditory stream segregation multiclass ERP (ASME) brain-computer interface task. Two strategies for achieving four classes were compared: ASME-4stream (four streams with one target stimulus each) and ASME-2stream (two streams with two target stimuli each). The recordings contain P300 responses to deviant tones and support offline binary classification and BCI simulation, with average accuracies of 0.83 and 0.86 for the two paradigms.
datasets.authors: Simon Kojima, Shin'ichiro Kanoh

datasets.name: Neuroergonomic 2021 dataset
datasets.description: This dataset contains 62-channel EEG recorded at 500 Hz from 15 healthy participants across two sessions. It combines resting-state recordings with three difficulty levels (easy, medium, difficult) of the MATB-II multitasking paradigm, and was designed for passive brain-computer interface research on cross-session mental workload estimation. The BIDS version is a MOABB-derived conversion of the COG-BCI database, with HED event annotations.
datasets.authors: Marcel F. Hinss, Emilie S. Jahanpour, Bertille Somon, Lou Pluchon, Frédéric Dehais, Raphaëlle N. Roy

datasets.name: RSVP collaborative BCI dataset from Zheng et al 2020
datasets.description: A cross-session EEG dataset for collaborative brain-computer interfaces based on rapid serial visual presentation (RSVP). Fourteen healthy participants, arranged in seven pairs, were recorded simultaneously over two sessions while detecting target images (humans vs. non-humans) in rapid image streams. The dataset contains 62-channel EEG with Target and NonTarget event annotations and supports P300/ERP and collaborative BCI research.
datasets.authors: Li Zheng, Sen Sun, Hongze Zhao, Weihua Pei, Hongda Chen, Xiaorong Gao, Lijian Zhang, Yijun Wang

datasets.name: Bluetooth speaker experiment (14 subjects, 6 classes, 31 EEG ch)
datasets.description: EEG recordings from 14 healthy participants performing a visual P300 oddball BCI task for controlling a Bluetooth speaker, one of several home appliances in the original study. The task used a 6-class flash-stimulus paradigm on an LCD display. Data were recorded from 31 channels at 500 Hz, with 50 training and 30 testing blocks per subject. The dataset supports research on ERP-based BCIs for home appliance control and inter-subject transfer learning.
datasets.authors: Jongmin Lee, Minju Kim, Dojin Heo, Jongsu Kim, Min-Ki Kim, Taejun Lee, Jongwoo Park, HyunYoung Kim, Minho Hwang, Laehyun Kim, Sung-Phil Kim

datasets.name: P300 dataset from initial spot study
datasets.description: An auditory oddball P300 EEG dataset from 13 healthy participants, recorded with 31 channels at 1000 Hz. Target (1000 Hz) and non-target (500 Hz) tones were presented at stimulus onset asynchronies from 60 to 600 ms. The dataset supports closed-loop optimization of stimulation speed in auditory brain-computer interfaces, using random search and Bayesian optimization to maximize regularized LDA classification performance.
datasets.authors: Jan Sosulski, David Hübner, Aaron Klein, Michael Tangermann

datasets.name: P300 dataset BI2012 from a "Brain Invaders" experiment
datasets.description: EEG recordings from 25 healthy volunteers playing Brain Invaders, a visual P300 brain-computer interface modeled on the video game Space Invaders. Data were acquired with 16 electrodes at GIPSA-lab (Grenoble, France) in 2012, using a training-test design with Target and NonTarget flashes. The dataset supports P300 BCI research and classification benchmarking, for example with xDAWN and Riemannian methods.
datasets.authors: G.F.P. Van Veen, A. Barachant, A. Andreev, G. Cattan, P. Rodrigues, M. Congedo

datasets.name: ERP paradigm of the Mobile BCI dataset
datasets.description: EEG recordings from 24 healthy participants performing a visual oddball (P300) event-related potential paradigm during mobile conditions: standing, walking, and running. Data were acquired with scalp and ear-EEG systems (73 channels, plus EOG) across five sessions per participant. This is a BIDS-formatted derivative of the Mobile BCI dataset, intended for benchmarking brain-computer interface decoding under locomotion.
datasets.authors: Young-Eun Lee, Gi-Hwan Shin, Minji Lee, Seong-Whan Lee

datasets.name: BigP3BCI Study I — 9x8 checkerboard/performance-based (13 healthy subjects)
datasets.description: This dataset contains EEG recordings from 13 healthy participants in Study I of the bigP3BCI collection. Participants used a P300-based speller with a 9x8 checkerboard character grid and a performance-based paradigm. Data were recorded from 16 channels at 256 Hz and are annotated with target and non-target stimulus events using HED. The dataset is a BIDS-formatted derivative of the PhysioNet bigP3BCI release, prepared for BCI benchmarking.
datasets.authors: Boyla Mainsah, Chance Fleeting, Thomas Balmat, Eric Sellers, Leslie Collins

datasets.name: Learning from label proportions for a visual matrix speller (ERP)
datasets.description: EEG recordings from 13 healthy participants performing an online copy-spelling task with a visual 6x7 matrix ERP speller. The speller was designed for learning from label proportions (LLP), an unsupervised, calibration-free classification approach for ERP-based brain-computer interfaces. Two stimulus sequences with different target/non-target ratios allowed the classifier to reconstruct mean target and non-target responses without labeled data. Participants spelled a German pangram three times, with 84.5% of characters spelled correctly on average without prior calibration.
datasets.authors: David Hübner, Thibault Verhoeven, Konstantin Schmid, Klaus-Robert Müller, Michael Tangermann, Pieter-Jan Kindermans

datasets.name: BNCI 2015-008 Center Speller P300 dataset
datasets.description: EEG recordings from 13 participants using a P300-based visual speller that relies on covert spatial attention and non-spatial feature attention (color and form), so users do not need to move their gaze. The study compared three speller variants (Hex-o-Spell, Cake Speller, Center Speller) in a calibration and online-test design. Data were recorded with 63 channels at 250 Hz, and event markers distinguish target from non-target intensifications.
datasets.authors: M S Treder, N M Schmidt, B Blankertz

datasets.name: BigP3BCI Study M — 9x8 adaptive/checkerboard (21 ALS subjects)
datasets.description: This dataset is a BIDS-formatted derivative of Study M from the bigP3BCI collection, a large open P300-based brain-computer interface resource. It contains 16-channel EEG recorded at 256 Hz from 21 participants using a 9x8 character speller grid with adaptive and checkerboard stimulus paradigms. Target and non-target events are annotated with HED tags, supporting machine-learning work on P300 speller classification.
datasets.authors: Boyla Mainsah, Chance Fleeting, Thomas Balmat, Eric Sellers, Leslie Collins

datasets.name: c-VEP dataset from Thielen et al. (2015)
datasets.description: A 64-channel EEG dataset from 12 healthy participants using a broad-band visually evoked potential (BBVEP) brain-computer interface with modulated Gold codes. Participants operated a 6x6 matrix speller in an online copy-spelling task, with each cell flashing according to pseudo-random bit-sequences. The dataset supports research on code-modulated VEP (c-VEP) BCIs and reconvolution-based template prediction. It is a preprocessed derivative distributed via MOABB.
datasets.authors: Jordy Thielen, Philip van den Broek, Jason Farquhar, Peter Desain

datasets.name: Mixture of LLP and EM for a visual matrix speller (ERP) dataset from
datasets.description: EEG recordings from an online study with twelve healthy participants using a visual matrix speller (P300 ERP) for copy-spelling. The study compared three unsupervised decoders: expectation-maximization, learning from label proportions, and their mixture (MIX). Recordings were made with 31 EEG channels at 1000 Hz. The data support research on calibration-free brain-computer interfaces based on event-related potentials.
datasets.authors: David Hübner, Thibault Verhoeven, Klaus-Robert Müller, Pieter-Jan Kindermans, Michael Tangermann

datasets.name: BNCI 2015-010 RSVP P300 dataset
datasets.description: EEG recordings from 12 healthy participants operating a gaze-independent rapid serial visual presentation (RSVP) P300 speller. Thirty symbols were shown one at a time at the center of the screen under three conditions (NoColor 116 ms SOA, Color 116 ms SOA, Color 83 ms SOA), each with calibration, copy-spelling and free-spelling phases. Online spelling reached a mean accuracy of 94.8% at 1.43 symbols/min, supporting use by patients with impaired oculo-motor control.
datasets.authors: Laura Acqualagna, Benjamin Blankertz

datasets.name: Kojima et al. 2024 (Dataset A) — An auditory brain-computer interface based on selective attention to multiple tone streams
datasets.description: This dataset contains 64-channel EEG and 2-channel EOG recordings from 11 healthy participants performing a three-class auditory brain-computer interface task based on auditory stream segregation. Musical piano tones were presented to the right ear as three tone streams, and participants attended to one stream while counting target (deviant) stimuli, which elicited P300 activity. Data were classified with Riemannian geometry and xDAWN spatial filtering, with cross-validated accuracy above 80% for five subjects and above 75% for nine subjects.
datasets.authors: Simon Kojima, Shin'ichiro Kanoh

datasets.name: BNCI 2015-006 Music BCI dataset
datasets.description: EEG recordings from 11 healthy participants performing a multi-streamed auditory oddball task with polyphonic music. Participants selectively attended to one of three concurrent instruments (Synth-Pop or Jazz clips) and counted deviants. The dataset supports brain-computer interface research on P300 and early auditory responses, and the attended instrument could be classified offline with a mean accuracy of 91%.
datasets.authors: M S Treder, H Purwins, D Miklody, I Sturm, B Blankertz

datasets.name: Sleep-EDF Expanded: Whole-Night PSG Recordings
datasets.description: A BIDS-formatted conversion of the PhysioNet Sleep-EDF Expanded database, containing 197 whole-night polysomnography recordings from about 100 subjects (some subjects contributed more than one night, so the number of recordings exceeds the number of subjects). It includes a cassette study of 78 healthy subjects with ambulatory recordings and a telemetry study of 22 subjects in a Temazepam drug study. Recordings include EEG, EOG and EMG channels, with expert-annotated 30-second sleep stage epochs in events files.
datasets.authors: Bob Kemp, Aeilko H. Zwinderman, Bert Tuk, Hilbert A.C. Kamphuisen, Josefien J.L. Oberye

datasets.name: NMT: Neurodiagnostic Montage Template Scalp EEG
datasets.description: A collection of 2,417 clinical scalp EEG recordings labeled as normal or abnormal, acquired using the standard 10-20 montage with 19 EEG channels plus 2 reference electrodes. Recordings are stored in EDF format with variable sampling rates and durations. The dataset supports EEG-based pathology detection and normal/abnormal classification.
datasets.authors: Hussain A. Khan

datasets.name: Brennan2019: EEG during Naturalistic Listening to Alice in Wonderland
datasets.description: Scalp EEG recorded from 45 participants listening to a 12.4-minute audiobook recording of the first chapter of Alice's Adventures in Wonderland. The naturalistic paradigm was designed to study how the brain builds hierarchical syntactic structure and makes rapid, incremental linguistic predictions. The dataset includes word-level events annotated with lexical frequency, sound power, and n-gram, RNN, and context-free-grammar surprisal predictors, along with comprehension scores and the audio stimuli.
datasets.authors: Jonathan R. Brennan, John T. Hale

datasets.name: LEMON: MPI Leipzig Mind-Brain-Body EEG (Resting State)
datasets.description: Resting-state EEG recorded from over 200 healthy young (20-35 years) and older (59-77 years) adults in the Leipzig Study for Mind-Body-Emotion Interactions (LEMON). Participants alternated between eyes-closed and eyes-open blocks of about 60 seconds over roughly 16 minutes. The data were recorded with a 62-channel active-electrode BrainVision system and restructured into BIDS-EEG layout.
datasets.authors: Anahit Babayan, Miray Erbey, Deniz Kumral, Janis D. Reinelt, Andrea M.F. Reiter, Josefin Röbbig, H. Lina Schaare, Marie Uhlig, Alfred Anwander, Pierre-Louis Bazin, Annette Horstmann, Leonie Lampe, Vadim V. Nikulin, Hadas Okon-Singer, Sven Preusser, Andre Pampel, Christiane S. Margulies, Michael Gaebler, Arno Villringer

datasets.name: Executive Functionning Study for Assessing the Effect of Neurofeedback
datasets.description: EEG recordings from an executive functioning battery comprising the N-Back, Sustained Attention to Response Task (SART), and Local-Global tasks. Data were collected from 24 participants in two sessions, on the first and last day of a frontal midline theta neurofeedback meditation training experiment, to assess neurofeedback effects on executive function. Data are provided in EEGLAB .set format, with the original .bdf files in the sourcedata folder.
datasets.authors: Arnaud Delorme, Tracy Brandmeyer

datasets.name: fNIRS Finger Tapping
datasets.description: An example functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) dataset from five participants performing a finger tapping task, organized according to the draft fNIRS BIDS specification. Participants tapped their left or right thumb to fingers, or rested as a control, in response to auditory cues, with sensors placed over the motor cortex and short channels attached. The dataset demonstrates conversion of NIRx recordings to BIDS using MNE-BIDS.
datasets.authors: Robert Luke, Eric Larson, Alexandre Gramfort, Macquarie University

datasets.name: MUniverse Grison et al 2025
datasets.description: High-density surface EMG (HDsEMG) recordings from the right tibialis anterior of a single healthy participant performing submaximal isometric ankle dorsiflexions at 10 to 70 percent of maximal voluntary contraction. Signals were acquired with two 64-electrode arrays (128 electrodes total) alongside force measurements. The dataset includes labeled motor unit spike trains derived from concurrent invasive EMG, and supports motor unit decomposition research.
datasets.authors: Agnese Grison, Irene Mendez Guerra, Alexander Kenneth Clarke, Silvia Muceli, Jaime Ibanez Pereda, Dario Farina

datasets.name: MUniverse Avrillon et al 2024
datasets.description: A BIDS-formatted high-density surface EMG (HDsEMG) dataset from 16 young volunteers performing submaximal (10-80% MVC) isometric ankle dorsiflexions (tibialis anterior, n=8) or knee extensions (vastus lateralis, n=8). Signals were recorded with four 64-electrode arrays (256 channels in total) together with force signals, supporting the decomposition of extensive motor unit samples and the study of rate coding. It is a BIDS conversion of the data from Avrillon et al. 2024, produced with the MUniverse software.
datasets.authors: Simon Avrillon, Francois Hug, Roger M. Enoka, Arnault H. Caillet, Dario Farina

datasets.name: MUniverse Caillet et al 2023
datasets.description: A BIDS-formatted dataset of high-density surface EMG (HDsEMG) recordings from the right tibialis anterior of six healthy male participants. Four 64-channel grids (256 electrodes) recorded trapezoidal isometric dorsiflexion contractions at 30% and 50% of maximal voluntary contraction, together with force signals. The dataset supports studies of electrode grid design and motor unit identification.
datasets.authors: Arnault H. Caillet, Simon Avrillon, Aritra Kundu, Tianyi Yu, Andrew T. M. Phillips, Luca Modenese, Dario Farina

datasets.name: BigP3BCI Study B — 6x6 checkerboard, multi-session (19 healthy subjects)
datasets.description: This dataset contains EEG recordings from 19 healthy participants from Study B of the bigP3BCI collection. Participants used a P300-based speller with a 6x6 checkerboard character grid over 8 sessions each. Data were recorded from 16 EEG channels at 256 Hz with a g.USBamp and annotated with HED tags for target and non-target events. The dataset is a MOABB-derived version of the bigP3BCI resource hosted on PhysioNet.
datasets.authors: Boyla Mainsah, Chance Fleeting, Thomas Balmat, Eric Sellers, Leslie Collins

datasets.name: RSVP ERP dataset for authentication from Zhang et al 2025
datasets.description: A longitudinal EEG dataset of event-related potentials recorded with a rapid serial visual presentation (RSVP) paradigm for EEG-based identity authentication. Fifteen healthy participants viewed streams of face images, with their own face as the target and AI-generated faces as non-targets, across four sessions spanning about 200 days. Recordings used 57 channels at 1000 Hz. The data support research on P300-based target detection and biometric authentication.
datasets.authors: Yufeng Zhang, Hongxin Zhang, Yixuan Li, Yijun Wang, Xiaorong Gao, Chen Yang

datasets.name: A COVID-19 survivors and close contacts EEG dataset
datasets.description: Resting-state EEG dataset from 169 participants, comprising 83 healthy close contacts and 86 COVID-19 survivors, collected at the Cuban Neuroscience Center. Recordings used the standard 10-20 montage and include eyes-closed resting EEG, alternating eyes-closed/open periods, and a recovery period. The dataset supports study of EEG signatures of COVID-19 survival relative to close contacts and the Cuban EEG normative database.
datasets.authors: Ana Calzada-Reyes, Eduardo Aubert-Vázquez, Lidice Galán-García, Maria Luisa Bringas-Vega, Trinidad Virués-Alba, Lidia Charroó-Ruiz, Yanely Acosta-Imás, Mitchell Valdés-Sosa, Laura Perez-Mayo, Joel Gutiérrez-Gil, Antonio Caballero-Moreno, Miguel Angel Alvarez, Norge Santiesteban, Javier Vicente Sánchez-Lopez, Annette Valdés-Virués, Elba Elvira Varona-Galindo, Elizabeth Méndez-Parra, Joviana Castro-Valiente, Leyanis Ramos-Hernández, Mabel Whilby-Santiesteban, Thelma Luz Carrillo-Alfonso, Shahwar Yasir, Yu Kin, Peng Ren, Dezhong Yao, Luo Cheng, Roberto Rodriguez-Labrada, Pedro Valdés-Sosa

datasets.name: Loneliness EEG - Roving Oddball Task
datasets.description: This dataset contains 64-channel EEG recordings from 99 young adults performing a visual roving oddball task with happy and angry face stimuli. Participants were grouped as lonely or non-lonely using the UCLA Loneliness Scale (Version 3) to test whether subjective loneliness is associated with altered automatic processing of social-emotional information, as indexed by ERP components. The dataset also includes post-session valence, arousal and dominance ratings of the faces, questionnaire measures, and preprocessed epoched derivatives.
datasets.authors: Joe Bathelt, Corine van Dijk, Marte Otten

datasets.name: Exo-EEG Experiment
datasets.description: EEG recordings from an experiment (Exo-EEG) on an exogenous task, collected at the University of Granada. The dataset is organized in BIDS format with participant information and task metadata provided in the accompanying files.
datasets.authors: Águeda Fuentes-Guerra, Elisa Martín Arévalo, Freek van Ede, Carlos González-García

datasets.name: tACS for Patients with Post-Stroke Anomia
datasets.description: EEG recordings from two chronic post-stroke anomia patients (one left-hemisphere and one right-hemisphere lesion) who took part in an 8-week individualized transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS) intervention. Stimulation and non-stimulation phases alternated every two weeks in a single-case ABAB design, with stimulation frequency and montage personalized from each patient's baseline EEG. EEG was recorded during a picture naming task at intervention and follow-up sessions to assess effects on naming accuracy and latency.
datasets.authors: Maria Martzoukou, Nefeli K. Dimitriou, Binbin Xu, Malo Renaud-d’Ambra, Anastasia Nousia, Alexandre Aksenov, Anne Beuter, Grigorios Nasios

datasets.name: Healthy Brain Network (HBN) EEG - Release 10
datasets.description: Release 10 of the HBN-EEG dataset, the EEG section of the Child Mind Institute Healthy Brain Network project, organized in BIDS format. It contains EEG recordings and behavioral responses from 533 participants aged 5-21 years performing six passive and active tasks (resting state, surround suppression, movie watching, contrast change detection, sequence learning, symbol search). Events carry HED annotations, and the participants file includes quality-control results and psychopathology factors derived from the CBCL.
datasets.authors: Seyed Yahya Shirazi, Alexandre Franco, Maurício Scopel Hoffmann, Nathalia B. Esper, Dung Truong, Arnaud Delorme, Michael Milham, Scott Makeig

datasets.name: Healthy Brain Network (HBN) EEG - Release 9
datasets.description: Release 9 of the HBN-EEG dataset, the EEG component of the Child Mind Institute Healthy Brain Network project, organized in BIDS. It contains EEG recordings and behavioral responses from 295 children and adolescents (ages 5-21) performing three passive tasks (resting state, surround suppression, movie watching) and three active tasks (contrast change detection, sequence learning, symbol search). Events carry HED annotations, and participants.tsv provides quality-control results and psychopathology factors derived from the CBCL, supporting research on pediatric mental health.
datasets.authors: Seyed Yahya Shirazi, Alexandre Franco, Maurício Scopel Hoffmann, Nathalia B. Esper, Dung Truong, Arnaud Delorme, Michael Milham, Scott Makeig

datasets.name: FFR-active-listening
datasets.description: EEG dataset titled 'FFR-active-listening', recorded in BrainVision format (.eeg/.vhdr/.vmrk) with accompanying BIDS metadata files (.json, .tsv, .csv). The title suggests a focus on frequency-following responses during active listening. The dataset comprises 249 files (226 GB). Detailed information on participants, tasks, stimuli, and acquisition parameters is not provided in the available documentation.
datasets.authors: [Unspecified]

datasets.name: Healthy Brain Network (HBN) EEG - Release 7
datasets.description: Release 7 of the HBN-EEG dataset, the EEG component of the Child Mind Institute Healthy Brain Network project, organized in BIDS format. It contains EEG recordings and behavioral responses from 381 participants aged 5-21 performing three passive tasks (resting state, surround suppression, movie watching) and three active tasks (contrast change detection, sequence learning, symbol search). Events carry HED annotations, and participants.tsv includes quality-control results and psychopathology factors derived from the CBCL questionnaire.
datasets.authors: Seyed Yahya Shirazi, Alexandre Franco, Maurício Scopel Hoffmann, Nathalia B. Esper, Dung Truong, Arnaud Delorme, Michael Milham, Scott Makeig

datasets.name: Healthy Brain Network (HBN) EEG - Release 5
datasets.description: Release 5 of the HBN-EEG dataset, the EEG component of the Child Mind Institute Healthy Brain Network, organized in BIDS format. It contains EEG recordings and behavioral responses from 330 children and adolescents (ages 5-21) performing passive tasks (resting state, surround suppression, movie watching) and active tasks (contrast change detection, sequence learning, symbol search). Events carry HED annotations, and the participants file includes psychopathology factors derived from the CBCL and basic quality-control results.
datasets.authors: Seyed Yahya Shirazi, Alexandre Franco, Maurício Scopel Hoffmann, Nathalia B. Esper, Dung Truong, Arnaud Delorme, Michael Milham, Scott Makeig

datasets.name: Healthy Brain Network (HBN) EEG - Release 4
datasets.description: Release 4 of the HBN-EEG dataset, the EEG section of the Child Mind Institute Healthy Brain Network project, organized in BIDS format. It contains EEG recordings and behavioral responses from 324 participants aged 5-21 years performing three passive tasks (resting state, surround suppression, movie watching) and three active tasks (contrast change detection, sequence learning, symbol search). Events carry HED annotations, and the participants file includes quality control results and psychopathology-related factors derived from the CBCL.
datasets.authors: Seyed Yahya Shirazi, Alexandre Franco, Maurício Scopel Hoffmann, Nathalia B. Esper, Dung Truong, Arnaud Delorme, Michael Milham, Scott Makeig

datasets.name: Healthy Brain Network (HBN) EEG - Release 8
datasets.description: Release 8 of the HBN-EEG dataset, the EEG component of the Child Mind Institute Healthy Brain Network project, organized in BIDS format. It contains EEG recordings and behavioral responses from 257 children and young adults (ages 5-21) performing six passive and active tasks: resting state, surround suppression, movie watching, contrast change detection, sequence learning, and symbol search. Events carry Hierarchical Event Descriptor (HED) annotations, and the participants file includes CBCL-derived psychopathology factors and quality-control results.
datasets.authors: Seyed Yahya Shirazi, Alexandre Franco, Maurício Scopel Hoffmann, Nathalia B. Esper, Dung Truong, Arnaud Delorme, Michael Milham, Scott Makeig

datasets.name: Structural MRI, Resting-state fMRI, and PSG/EEG Dataset of Zoster-associated Neuralgia
datasets.description: This dataset contains anatomical T1-weighted MRI, raw multi-echo resting-state fMRI, and polysomnography (PSG) EEG recordings from healthy controls and patients with zoster-associated neuralgia (ZAN). It supports investigation of brain structure, functional activity, and sleep differences between HC and ZAN groups. MRI and PSG data partly overlap across participants, and sleep stages were manually scored according to AASM criteria.
datasets.authors: Li Li, Qi Han, Haolei Bai, Xiaolong Zhang, Yong Liu, Chao He
